chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: 'Among the happiness of a Muslim man is a comfortable mount.'

key_terms.الْمَرْكَبُ: Mount, riding animal (horse, camel, mule) — the primary means of transport in classical Arabia
key_terms.الْهَنِيءُ: Comfortable, pleasant, wholesome — denoting a well-trained, gentle riding animal
key_terms.سَعَادَة: Happiness, felicity, good fortune — a comprehensive state of wellbeing

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about the happiness of a Muslim man?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates a saying of the Prophet (SAWW) that identifies a comfortable riding animal as one of the sources of happiness for a Muslim. This hadith is part of the chapter on the bond between an animal and its rider, reflecting the 7th-century Arabian context where a reliable, well-tempered horse or camel was a practical necessity and a mark of one's ease in travel and daily life. The Arabic word 'hani' (هَنِيء) conveys not just physical comfort but wholesomeness and pleasantness.
